title: Critical Data Question 1
scenario: Imagine a giant ice cube floating in a glass of water. If that ice cube melts, the level stays the same.
question: Now think about Arctic sea ice floating in the ocean. If this floating sea ice melts completely, what happens to sea level?

options.text: The sea level will rise significantly
options.explanation: People assume melting ice always adds volume, but floating ice already displaces its own weight!

options.text: It adds a lot of extra water to the ocean
options.explanation: Just like in a glass, floating ice has already displaced the water, so melting doesnt add extra volume.

options.text: The sea level stays about the same
options.explanation: Melting adds liquid water to the surface: it does not remove water from the ocean.

title: Critical Data Question 2
scenario: Satellite records show Arctic sea-ice area shrinking in every recent decade.
question: What does less bright ice at the surface do to how much sunlight Earth absorbs?

options.text: Earth reflects more sunlight, so cooling increases
options.explanation: Less ice means more dark ocean, which absorbs more sunlight and can amplify warming.

options.text: Earth absorbs more sunlight, which can amplify warming
options.explanation: Less ice means more dark ocean, which absorbs more sunlight and can amplify warming.

options.text: It has no measurable impact on energy balance
options.explanation: Less ice means more dark ocean, which absorbs more sunlight and can amplify warming.

title: Critical Data Question 3
scenario: Permafrost stores large amounts of frozen organic carbon across Arctic land.
question: When permafrost thaws, which climate effect is most likely?

options.text: Long-term greenhouse gas release can increase
options.explanation: Thawing permafrost releases stored carbon, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions.
Thawing permafrost releases stored carbon, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions.

options.text: Only ocean salinity changes, not climate
options.explanation: Thawing permafrost releases stored carbon, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Critical Data Question 4
scenario: The Arctic warms several times faster than the global average.
question: Which action helps reduce future warming pressure the most?

options.text: Higher fossil fuel use for short-term growth
options.explanation: Using more fossil fuels increases greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to global warming.
Delaying clean energy adoption prolongs reliance on fossil fuels, increasing emissions.

options.text: Reducing emissions through efficiency and clean energy
options.explanation: Implementing energy efficiency measures and transitioning to clean energy sources reduces greenhouse gas emissions, mitigating future warming.
